tagline: A river-commuter megacity with a Gulf of islands within hybrid reach.
summary: Bangkok runs on the Chao Phraya — one of the world's busiest urban river-transit systems — while the Gulf of Thailand puts Pattaya, Koh Chang and Koh Samui within reach. Pioneer II suits the river and inner-gulf corridors; Quanta-LR opens the long gulf-island runs as single legs.

demand_signals.label: Megacity congestion
demand_signals.note: Water already relieves the road network; a premium tier extends it

demand_signals.label: Gulf-island tourism
demand_signals.note: High-demand island destinations reached today by slow ferry/air

demand_signals.label: Super-app density
demand_signals.note: Demand lives in-app; the water tier is unclaimed

use_cases.title: Premium river tier
use_cases.body: A quiet, zero-emission foiling service on the Chao Phraya above the existing express-boat network — fast, smooth, premium.

use_cases.title: Branded water tier
use_cases.body: In-app premium river and inner-gulf hops, relieving the city's chronic road congestion.

use_cases.title: Gulf-island corridors
use_cases.body: Bangkok / Pattaya to Koh Chang and Koh Samui as fast, comfortable runs that conventional ferries make slow and rough.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: All-electric river and inner-gulf corridors with berth-pedestal charging — a premium layer on a mature water-commuting culture.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Opens the long gulf-island runs — Bangkok / Pattaya to Koh Samui (~205 nm) and Koh Chang — as single hybrid legs with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

transit_planning: For an authority: a premium, zero-emission tier above the mature Chao Phraya network, plus credible gulf-island corridors — additive to existing river transit and relieving road congestion.

grab.note: A branded river-and-gulf water tier in a megacity where demand already lives in-app.
